 'Winning mentality becomes contagious' published at 20:13 GMT 20:13 GMT 
 FT: Sparta Prague 1-3 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth midfielder Tyler Adams talking to TNT Sports on what it feels like to win a seventh game in a row: "Like hard work, this team [Sparta Prague] is very organised and has a lot of quality. I don’t want to say we weren’t ready for the game but they brought a lot of energy. 
 "When you are playing every three days, it was nice to give guys an opportunity and show the depth of our squad. 
 "To bring guys on later and bring that energy, showed what we are capable of. 
 "Obviously good [to score] but the win is the most important thing, I am just glad to have an impact."
 On Evanilson's form: "He’s on fire right now, you see him work on it in training, he does extra work on his finishing every day after training so for him to do it in a game is no surprise. 
 "He has so much quality, so whenever he gets in and around the box we are confident that is going to find the back of the net."
 On seven-game winning run: "Can’t get too comfortable. You have to be able to hold that winning standard, that winning mentality becomes contagious especially when you are playing every three days. 
 "It doesn’t feel that long ago since we lost 5-1 to Chelsea and that stings a little bit, we don’t want to feel that ever again. I think we turned a page and we have been a more mature team ever since that; the way that we defend, the way that we take pride in the mentality of making sure we don’t give the opposition any opportunity to breathe. 
 "Everyone is working hard every day in training, guys that aren’t playing are working hard, the guys that are playing are working hard so there’s a lot of competition but that breathes success. I’m happy with the team’s performance."

 By Chris McKenna BBC Sport journalist Marco Rose used his bench to inspire Bournemouth to come from behind against 10-man Sparta Prague and maintain their 100% record in the Europa League this season. 
 Tyler Adams, Evanilson and Rayan all came on as substitutes to score as the Cherries made it four wins from four in their debut European campaign.
 American midfielder Adams got the equaliser soon after the break, to cancel out Ebrima Singhateh's first-half opener, when he finished well after Amine Adli had sparked a move by pouncing on a mistake from the Czech side's defence.
 It followed Tobias Guddal being sent off for Sparta in the first half for a second yellow card.
 The Cherries had to wait until nine minutes to go to get the second, Evanilson providing a superb finish from inside the area to put them ahead before Rayan scored the third with an effort from just outside the box.
 Bournemouth boss Rose made eight changes from their weekend win over Leeds United and the visitors struggled early on in Prague.
 Jonatan Braut Brunes missed a great opportunity in the opening moments before Bournemouth's Lewis Cook hit the post with a penalty following a handball from former Liverpool and Wolves defender Ki-Jana Hoever.
 Sparta took a deserved lead in the 35th minute after some brilliant footwork from Singhateh, who used a clever trick to beat Adam Smith and Cook in one movement before delivering a brilliant finish.
 The Czech side's joy was short-lived as two minutes later they were reduced to 10 men as defender Guddal was sent off for a second bookable offence, for pulling down Alvaro Rodriguez.
 That certainly took the momentum from the hosts and Rose opted to bring on some of his regulars as Adams was the first substitute at the interval. 
 He had an immediate impact, with his energy reinvigorating Bournemouth, and got his goal 12 minutes after the restart.
 Rose then continued to make changes with Evanilson, Adrien Truffert, Marcus Tavernier and Rayan all coming off the bench as they penned in Sparta looking for the winning goal but squandered chances.
 But they got the important goals late on to make it seven wins in a row in all competitions.
 What did you make of Bournemouth’s display?
